messages.text: LeBron held to single digits for only 10th time on Cleveland return

metadata.summary: LeBron James was held to single-digit points for only the 10th time in 1,630 NBA regular-season games as his Philadelphia 76ers were beaten on his return to face his former team the Cleveland Cavaliers.
metadata.content: NBA: LeBron James held to single-digit points for only 10th time as Philadelphia 76ers lose to Cleveland Cavaliers | NBA News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NBA: LeBron James held to single-digit points for only 10th time as Philadelphia 76ers lose to Cleveland Cavaliers LeBron James held to eight points as Philadelphia 76ers lose 119-95 on his return to Cleveland; the 41-year-old received smattering of boos from Cavaliers fans during first half; James spent 11 seasons over two stints with the Cavs Saturday 7 November 2026 08:06, UK Image: LeBron James has been held to less than 10 points only 10 times in 1,630 NBA regular-season games LeBron James was held to single-digit points for only the 10th time in 1,630 NBA regular-season games as his Philadelphia 76ers were beaten on his return to face his former team the Cleveland Cavaliers. James was held to eight points as the Cavaliers routed the 76ers 119-95 in an NBA Cup group stage game. The 41-year-old, a native of Akron, Ohio, who elected to sign with Philadelphia in the offseason, instead of returning to Cleveland for a third stint, was 3 of 12 from the field, including 0 for 4 on three-pointers, while he committed six turnovers in 31 minutes. messages.text: Fritz misses out on ATP Finals after squandering chance to beat Alcaraz

metadata.summary: Taylor Fritz missed out on claiming the last spot at the ATP Finals in Turin later this month after squandering two match points in his Paris Masters quarter-final defeat to Carlos Alcaraz.
metadata.content: Paris Masters: Taylor Fritz squanders match points against Carlos Alcaraz as defeat ends hopes of reaching ATP Finals | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Paris Masters: Taylor Fritz squanders match points against Carlos Alcaraz as defeat ends hopes of reaching ATP Finals Season-ending ATP Finals live on Sky Sports from November 15-22 , with Spanish youngster Rafael Jodar taking eighth and final spot after Taylor Fritz's defeat to already-qualified Carlos Alcaraz in Paris; Frances Tiafoe's place secured earlier on Friday Saturday 7 November 2026 00:20, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from a thrilling quarter-final at the Paris Masters as Carlos Alcaraz fought from a set down to beat Taylor Fritz Taylor Fritz missed out on claiming the last spot at the ATP Finals in Turin later this month after squandering two match points in his Paris Masters quarter-final defeat to Carlos Alcaraz. Fritz would have reached the end-of-season event in Italy at Rafael Jodar's expense had he beaten Alcaraz to make the last four. He looked poised to do that after twice finding himself a point from victory in the second set, once on his opponent's serve at 5-3 up and then on his own with the score at 5-4. However, Alcaraz rallied during a high-quality match to triumph 6-7 (10-12) 7-5 6-3 and ensure he will be joined by compatriot Jodar at the ATP Finals from November 15-22, live on Sky Sports . messages.text: Leclerc plans 'significant' car changes after tough day for Ferrari

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc says he will make "significant" setup changes to his car after "one of the worst feelings" in practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Charles Leclerc plans 'significant' Ferrari car changes as Lewis Hamilton rues 'difficult' Brazil practice | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Charles Leclerc plans 'significant' Ferrari car changes as Lewis Hamilton rues 'difficult' Brazil practice Ferrari were off the pace compared to Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull on Friday in Brazil with both Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton unhappy about the car's balance; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead Qualifying at 6pm live on Sky Sports F1 on Saturday Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Friday 6 November 2026 22:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix Charles Leclerc says he will make "significant" setup changes to his car after "one of the worst feelings" in practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Leclerc was seven tenths off pace-setter Kimi Antonelli in second practice and Lewis Hamilton was nearly half a second behind as Ferrari trailed Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull on Friday. It was a contrast to their recent pace with Ferrari claiming a podium position in the last four races but Leclerc is hoping they can turn that around in final practice on Saturday at 2.30pm and qualifying at 6pm, live on Sky Sports F1 . messages.text: New champion Antonelli tops Brazil practice

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli completed an impressive first day back on track as F1's new world champion to set the pace in second practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest for Mercedes in second practice at Interlagos ahead of Lando Norris in upgraded McLaren | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest for Mercedes in second practice at Interlagos ahead of Lando Norris in upgraded McLaren F1's new world champion sets the pace from its outgoing one on the first day in Brazil; Max Verstappen third fastest but Ferraris off pace on short runs; Rain forecast over weekend; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead Qualifying at 6pm live on Sky Sports F1 on Saturday Saturday 7 November 2026 08:43, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Kimi Antonelli completed an impressive first day back on track as F1's new world champion to set the pace in second practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Five days after becoming the sport's youngest title winner in Mexico, Antonelli followed up his second-fastest time from first practice with the quickest of the more representative second session around the undulating Interlagos lap. Antonelli was the only driver to lap below 71 seconds with his benchmark time of 1:10.763 proving two tenths of a second quicker than nearest challengers Lando Norris, the P1 pacesetter , and Max Verstappen.
